sections.heading: Part I — Student-Produced Response Questions (SPRs): Foundational Fluency (1–7)

questions.target: Area, Volume, Similar Triangles, Circles & Right-Triangle Trig
questions.q: A right triangle has legs of length 6 and 8. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
questions.answer: **Answer:** \(10\). By the Pythagorean theorem: \(c = \sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = \sqrt{36 + 64} = \sqrt{100} = 10\).

questions.target: Area, Volume, Similar Triangles, Circles & Right-Triangle Trig
questions.q: parallel lines \(p\) and \(q\) crossed by a brace form supplementary angles \(56^\circ\) and \((4m + 24)^\circ\); determine \(m\). Such behavior characterizes precision offset printing rollers (pages) logged during estimating maintenance intervals.
questions.answer: **Answer:** \(25\). **Algebraic Method:** \((4m + 24) + 56 = 180 \Rightarrow m = 25\). **Desmos Strategy:** Graph both equations against 180. **Trap Watchout:** Supplementary angles add to 180 rather than equaling each other.

questions.target: Area, Volume, Similar Triangles, Circles & Right-Triangle Trig
questions.q: Suppose laboratory records from industrial campus electric shuttles (miles) show the allocation while inspecting experimental logs: the illustrated conical hopper holds radius \(12\) and altitude \(27\); if volume writes as \(h\pi\), compute \(h\).
questions.answer: **Answer:** \(1296\). **Algebraic Method:** Volume formula gives \(1296\pi\), hence \(h = 1296\). **Desmos Strategy:** Compute exact integer/rational coefficient directly. **Trap Watchout:** Square only the radius and keep 1/3 for cones.

questions.target: Area, Volume, Similar Triangles, Circles & Right-Triangle Trig
questions.q: Technical documentation covering offshore induction foundry crucibles (forecasting seasonal demand) specifies the relationship: determine hypotenuse length \(YZ\) when \(\triangle XYZ\) meets at \(\angle X=90^\circ\) with legs \(10\) and \(24\).
questions.answer: **Answer:** \(26\). **Algebraic Method:** \(\sqrt{10^2 + 24^2} = 26\). **Desmos Strategy:** Evaluate `sqrt(10^2 + 24^2)` in Desmos. **Trap Watchout:** Always square both legs before adding.

questions.target: Geometry & Trigonometry
questions.q: Based on urban agricultural seed vaults telemetry collected while assessing capacity thresholds, compute complementary trigonometric value \(\cos J\) using legs \(9, 12\) and hypotenuse \(15\).
questions.answer: **Answer:** \(4/5\). **Algebraic Method:** Opposite side over hypotenuse gives \(\frac{4}{5}\). **Desmos Strategy:** Simplify `12/15` via the fraction toggle. **Trap Watchout:** Match opposite and adjacent relative to the specified angle.

questions.target: Geometry & Trigonometry
questions.q: When reviewing field logs of municipal transformer substations collected while tracking inventory movement, a circle centered at \(O\) shows radius \(21\) and sector angle \(160^\circ\); if minor arc equals \(k\pi\), solve for \(k\).
questions.answer: **Answer:** \(56/3\). **Algebraic Method:** \(\frac{160}{360} \cdot 2\pi(21) = \frac{56}{3}\pi\), so \(k = \frac{56}{3}\). **Desmos Strategy:** Evaluate `(160/360)*2*21`. **Trap Watchout:** Use circumference \(2\pi r\) for arc length, not \(\pi r^2\).

questions.target: Geometry & Trigonometry
questions.q: Consider this hydraulic container barge terminals distribution profile gathered while documenting yield ratios. Namely, parallel lines \(p\) and \(q\) crossed by a brace form supplementary angles \(61^\circ\) and \((2w + 59)^\circ\); determine \(w\).
questions.answer: **Answer:** \(30\). **Algebraic Method:** \((2w + 59) + 61 = 180 \Rightarrow w = 30\). **Desmos Strategy:** Graph both equations against 180. **Trap Watchout:** Supplementary angles add to 180 rather than equaling each other.

questions.target: Geometry & Trigonometry
questions.q: Two vertical poles stand \(24\) meters apart on level ground, with heights \(10\) meters and \(17\) meters. What is the straight-line distance in meters between their tops?
questions.answer: **Answer:** \(25\). Horizontal gap \(24\), vertical difference \(17 - 10 = 7\); hypotenuse \(\sqrt{24^2 + 7^2} = 25\).

questions.q: What is the surface area of a cube with edge length 4 cm?
questions.answer: A cube has 6 congruent square faces: \(SA = 6s^2 = 6(4^2) = 6(16) = 96 \text{ cm}^2\).

questions.q: What is the area of a parallelogram with base 12 cm and height 5 cm?
questions.answer: \(\text{Area} = \text{base} \times \text{height} = 12 \times 5 = 60 \text{ cm}^2\).

questions.q: In right triangle \(XYZ\) with \(\angle Z = 90^\circ\), if \(\tan X = \frac{7}{24}\), what is \(\sin X\)?
questions.answer: **Answer:** \(\frac{7}{25}\). Opposite \(= 7\), adjacent \(= 24\), hypotenuse \(= \sqrt{7^2 + 24^2} = 25\), so \(\sin X = 7/25\).

questions.q: A rectangle has a width of 7 cm and a diagonal of 25 cm. What is the length of the rectangle?
questions.answer: By the Pythagorean theorem: \(l = \sqrt{25^2 - 7^2} = \sqrt{625 - 49} = \sqrt{576} = 24 \text{ cm}\).

questions.q: In a right triangle with legs 5 and 12, what is \(\tan(\theta)\) if \(\theta\) is opposite the leg of length 5?
questions.answer: \(\tan(\theta) = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}} = \frac{5}{12}\).

questions.q: Line \(PT\) is tangent to a circle with center \(O\) at point \(T\). If \(OT = 9\) and \(OP = 41\), what is length \(PT\)?
questions.answer: **Answer:** \(40\). Tangent meets radius at \(90^\circ\), so \(PT = \sqrt{41^2 - 9^2} = \sqrt{1600} = 40\).

questions.target: Geometry & Trigonometry
questions.q: If a sphere’s radius triples, by what factor does its volume increase?
questions.answer: **Answer:** \(27\). Volume is proportional to \(r^3\), so \(3^3 = 27\).
